title: Practice: how greedy, ε-greedy and UCB choose
note: Three problems since 2026-11-05, greedy and UCB only (ε-greedy left out of the lesson): P3 (greedy against UCB after an unlucky start), P4 (which option UCB picks in one round) and P2 (what one pick does to every score). P1, P5 and P6 need ε-greedy and are marked off: kept, never served. Two rounds of three problems, from the team's item design (P1 to P6). Round 2 repeats round 1's facts in new settings (P4 repeats P2's, P5 P1's and adds UCB, P6 P3's over many rounds), so a correction in round 1 can carry over. Options state only the prediction. Answers and worked solutions stay on the server and are shown on the results page after the final test. Each solution step lists the facts it relies on. `needs` lists the teachable facts without which the answer can't be reached, in the order the steps use them: in the recursive condition Kai can only be right when its notebook holds all of them, correctly explained. Given facts (the setup, averages, trying each option once) are never needed: Kai knows them and the stems repeat them. `beliefs` give, for each needed fact, the answer Kai's assumption for that fact leads to (the fact's `assume` in the graph, word for word; `when: vague` for how Kai reads a vague explanation, where that differs). When needed facts are missing, Kai reasons from the assumption of the first one in `needs` order whose assumption leads somewhere wrong, says that it is guessing, and its wrong answer follows from its own steps. Every wrong option is the prediction of a named misconception (Kai's or a known learner one), so no option can be ruled out without the facts.

items.title: Two cakes
items.prompt: Two cafés test the same two new cakes and score each day's sales out of 10. Cake A is truly better: its days usually score between 7 and 9. Cake B's days always score between 5 and 7. On the first two days both cafés try each cake once; in both, A has an unusually bad day (3) and B scores 6. From then on café 1 uses greedy and café 2 uses UCB. Which café ends up selling mostly cake A?
options: Both cafés
Neither café
Only café 1
Only café 2

steps.text: After the first two days, A's average is 3 and B's is 6.
Greedy picks B. B's days score 5 to 7, so B's average stays above 3, greedy never picks A again, and A's average stays at 3.
UCB adds a bonus. Each day B is picked, B's bonus shrinks.
Each day A is not picked, A's bonus grows.
So A's score eventually passes B's, UCB tries A again, A's average rises towards 8, and UCB then mostly sells A.

beliefs.belief: If greedy keeps going, the averages correct themselves over time, so greedy finds the best option in the end.
Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.
An option's bonus stays the same while it is not picked.
The bonus of an option that is not picked grows at a steady rate, so a neglected option comes back at regular intervals.
UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.

items.title: Audio tours
items.prompt: A museum app suggests one of four audio tours with UCB. All of the following is for the same round. Tour A averages 6.0 (suggested 50 times), B 6.4 (10 times), C 5.0 (10 times) and D 6.4 (40 times). Which tour does UCB suggest next?
options: B or D
B
B or C
It cannot be told without the bonus values

steps.text: UCB suggests the tour with the highest average plus bonus.
A tour's bonus shrinks with every suggestion, so in the same round fewer suggestions means a larger bonus.
B against D: same average, B suggested less, so B scores higher. B against C: same suggestions and so the same bonus, and B has the higher average. B against A: higher average and fewer suggestions.
So B has the highest score, without computing any bonus.

beliefs.belief: UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.
Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.

items.title: Exercise types
items.prompt: A language app picks the next exercise type with UCB. Before this round: Flashcards average 6.3, bonus 1.0 (tried 20 times); Dialogues average 5.0, bonus 2.5 (tried 3 times); Listening average 4.0, bonus 1.5 (tried 8 times). UCB picks Dialogues, and the learner scores exactly 5.0 on it. What happens to the three scores (average plus bonus) for the next round?
options: Dialogues' score falls; the other two rise slightly
All three scores fall slightly
Dialogues' score falls; the other two stay the same
All three scores stay the same

steps.text: The scores were Flashcards 7.3, Dialogues 7.5 and Listening 5.5, so UCB picked Dialogues.
The new result equals Dialogues' average, so the average stays 5.0.
Dialogues was tried once more, so its bonus shrinks and its score falls.
Flashcards and Listening were not picked, so their bonuses grow slightly with the round number.

beliefs.belief: Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.
An option's bonus stays the same while it is not picked.
The bonus of an option that is not picked grows at a steady rate, so a neglected option comes back at regular intervals.

items.title: Festival stages
items.prompt: A festival app recommends one of four stages to each visitor with ε-greedy, ε = 0.2. Ratings so far: stage A averages 7.8 (200 visitors), B 7.5 (3 visitors), C 4.0 (150 visitors) and D 6.9 (180 visitors). Assume A stays the favourite. Of the next 1,000 visitors, about how many are sent to A, and how do B and C compare?
options: About 800 to A; B and C about equally often
About 800 to A; B much more often than C
About 850 to A; B and C about equally often
Nearly all to A; B and C almost never

steps.text: A has the highest average, so in 80% of rounds (800 visitors) the app sends people to A.
In the other 20% (200 visitors) it picks at random; ε stays at 0.2 however reliable A's average is.
A random pick chooses each of the four stages with equal chance, A included: 50 more to A, and 50 each to B, C and D.
So about 850 go to A, and B and C come up equally often.

beliefs.belief: ε-greedy explores less and less once its averages become reliable.
When ε-greedy picks at random, it chooses among the options other than the favourite.

items.title: Page layouts
items.prompt: An online shop tests four product-page layouts. Click rates so far: A 12% (2,000 shows), B 11% (30 shows), C 2% (2,000 shows) and D 10% (2,500 shows). Shop 1 uses ε-greedy and shop 2 uses UCB, and both have this same history. Which layouts could each shop show in the next round?
options: Shop 1: any of the four; shop 2: A or B
Shop 1: A or B; shop 2: A or B
Shop 1: any of the four; shop 2: only B
Shop 1: any of the four; shop 2: any of the four

steps.text: Shop 1 shows A when it does not pick at random.
A random pick can land on any of the four layouts, so shop 1 could show any of them.
Shop 2 shows the highest average plus bonus.
C has as many shows as A, so the same bonus, and a lower average. D has more shows than A, so a smaller bonus, and a lower average. Neither can beat A.
B has a lower average than A but far fewer shows, so a larger bonus; which of the two wins depends on the bonus sizes. So shop 2 shows A or B.

beliefs.belief: UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.
The bonus adapts to how much an option's observed rewards vary.

items.title: Thumbnails
items.prompt: A video site picks one of five thumbnails for each of 1,000,000 visitors. Site 1 uses ε-greedy with ε = 0.1 and site 2 uses UCB. Thumbnail E is clearly the worst, and after the first 10,000 visitors both sites' averages show this. How often is E shown to visitors 10,001 to 20,000 compared with visitors 990,001 to 1,000,000?
options: Both sites show E much less often in the later period
Both sites show E about as often in both periods
Site 1 about as often in both periods; site 2 much less often later
Site 1 about as often in both periods; site 2 not at all later

steps.text: Site 1 makes a random pick with the same probability, 0.1, early and late.
Each random pick lands on E with the same chance, 1 in 5, so E goes to about 2% of visitors in both periods.
Site 2 shows E only when E's score beats all others, and every show of E shrinks E's bonus.
While E is not shown, its bonus grows again, but ever more slowly as rounds pass.
So the gaps between E's shows keep growing, and E is shown much less often later.

beliefs.belief: ε-greedy explores less and less once its averages become reliable.
UCB picks the option it is least sure about, the one tried the fewest times, whatever its average.
Every bonus shrinks as rounds pass, whether its option is picked or not.
An option's bonus stays the same while it is not picked.
The bonus of an option that is not picked grows at a steady rate, so a neglected option comes back at regular intervals.
